proof.text: Write $V=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and $H=\Lambda_k^n$. By the horn definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], a monotone string belongs to $H$ exactly when it omits some vertex $j\ne k$: it then factors through the included face omitting $j$, and conversely every string in that face omits $j$. A strictly increasing string thus fails to belong to $H$ exactly when its vertex set is $V$ or $V\setminus\{k\}$. Denote these strings by $t=[0,\ldots,n]$ and $u=[0,\ldots,\widehat k,\ldots,n]$. Let $A_r\subset P(n)_r$ be the free span of all other strict strings. Every sub-string of a horn string still omits the same $j\ne k$, so the displayed boundary formula of [lem-cbc-normalized-simplex-chain-diagonal] makes $A$ a subcomplex.

proof.text: The degreewise free-module inclusion $\Lambda[H]\to F(n)$ is injective: distinct horn strings remain distinct basis vectors. Normalization restricts this inclusion to the positive-face kernels, by [lem-cbc-dold-kan-normalization-equivalence], so $i$ is degreewise injective. Compose with the chain isomorphism $q_n:B\to P(n)$ of [lem-cbc-normalized-simplex-chain-diagonal]. Since $q_n$ discards noninjective strings, $q_ni(K_r)\subset A_r$. Conversely, each basis string $v$ of $A_r$ omits some $j\ne k$, hence is $P(\delta_j)(v_0)$ for a unique strict string $v_0$ in $P(n-1)_r$. Put $x_0=q_{n-1}^{-1}(v_0)$. The face map $F(n-1)\to\Lambda[H]$ takes $x_0$ into $K_r$, since it commutes with all positive faces. Naturality of the stated $q$ gives $q_ni(N(\delta_j)(x_0))=P(\delta_j)(v_0)=v$. Extending linearly gives every element of $A_r$. Thus $q_ni:K\to A$ is a degreewise bijective chain map, hence an isomorphism: its inverse commutes with the differential by composing the chain-map equation with the inverse on each side.

proof.text: Use $q_n$ and the preceding identification to work with $A\subset P(n)$. The quotient in each degree has just the remaining basis vectors: the class of $t$ in degree $n$ and the class of $u$ in degree $n-1$. Set $\sigma=(-1)^k$. The boundary formula of [lem-cbc-normalized-simplex-chain-diagonal] gives $\partial t=\sigma u+h$, where $h=\sum_{j\ne k}(-1)^j[0,\ldots,\widehat j,\ldots,n]\in A_{n-1}$. Every face of $u$ lies in $A$ when $n>1$, while for $n=1$ its differential is zero because it has degree zero. Hence the quotient differential is multiplication by $\sigma$ and all other differentials are zero. This proves the specified quotient description without changing its sign.

proof.text: Put $b=\partial t=\sigma u+h$. Define $s:D^n\to P(n)$ by sending the standard generator in degree $n$ to $t$ and the standard generator in degree $n-1$ to $b$, with zero maps in all other degrees. This is a chain map: $\partial t=b$, $\partial b=\partial^2t=0$, and these are exactly the two equations for the disk differential, including $n=1$. The map $\Phi:A\oplus D^n\to P(n)$, $(a,z)\mapsto a+s(z)$, is degreewise invertible. Indeed, in degree $n$ it sends the disk generator to the only basis vector $t$. In degree $n-1$, write an element uniquely as $a+c u$; its inverse is $(a-\sigma c h,\sigma c)$ since $\sigma^2=1$. In every other degree it is the identity on $A$. The inverse of this bijective chain map is again a chain map by its commuting-differential equation. Thus $\Phi$ is an isomorphism of complexes.

proof.text: Transport $\Phi$ along the isomorphism $K\cong A$ from step 2 and $q_n^{-1}:P(n)\to B$. The resulting isomorphism $K\oplus D^n\cong B$ restricts on $K$ to $i$, since $q_ni$ is precisely the inclusion of the identified $A$. Its inverse followed by projection onto $K$ is a chain map $r:B\to K$ with $ri=\mathrm{id}_K$. This proves that $i$ is a split monomorphism, as well as the requested direct-sum statement.

title: Normalized free horn quotient is a two-term disk
statement: Fix a commutative ring $\Lambda$, an integer $n\geq1$ and $0\leq k\leq n$. Use simplicial sets and horns as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the normalization $N$ on simplicial $\Lambda$-modules from [lem-cbc-dold-kan-normalization-equivalence]. For a simplicial set $S$, let $\Lambda[S]$ be the simplicial module freely generated in each degree by $S$ in that degree, with operators induced linearly. Put $K=N\Lambda[\Lambda_k^n]$ and $B=N\Lambda[\Delta^n]$, and let $i:K\to B$ be induced by the horn inclusion. Let $D^n$ be the nonnegative chain complex with a free rank-one module in degrees $n$ and $n-1$, zero in other degrees, and differential the identity from degree $n$ to degree $n-1$. Then $i$ is a split monomorphism of chain complexes, and there is an isomorphism $K\oplus D^n\cong B$ carrying the summand inclusion of $K$ to $i$. Under the natural nondegenerate-string model $P(n)$ of [lem-cbc-normalized-simplex-chain-diagonal], $K$ is the subcomplex spanned by every strictly increasing string except the top string $[0,\ldots,n]$ and the omitted face $[0,\ldots,\widehat k,\ldots,n]$. These two classes freely generate $B/iK$ in degrees $n$ and $n-1$, respectively, with differential $(-1)^k$ between them.
